decisions.reason: The reference-class electrometer sits in the firm's core dosimetry business, is featured on the home page, and appears to meet aspirations, so there is no trigger for problemistic search.

Oncology risk management software lies further from the hardware core and its results are less certain, but it is still kept on its own page and the firm's slack lets it carry the product while it builds adoption in clinics.
The CT image quality phantom is a recent launch that fits closely with the established medical imaging QA line, so it is too early to judge it against aspirations and it should be retained.
The mammography phantom serves a regulated, steady demand for QA in screening programmes and is just one year old, so keeping it is justified.
The full field mammography phantom overlaps somewhat with Product D, but it serves a distinct test need and costs little to carry, so it is retained.
This broad imaging QA instrument line extends the core business and shows no evidence of shortfall, so it is kept.
